newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Credit Bank shares drop to new year low.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Credit Bank shares drop to new year low.

text.p: Shares in Nippon Credit Bank Ltd, a Japanese long-term credit bank, dropped to their lowest level for the current financial year on Wednesday,
As of 0052 GMT, the bank's share price was down 16 yen at 200 yen, making it the fourth biggest percentage loser on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Volume was 4.002 million shares.
The shares had briefly dipped to 199 yen.
The level was lower than the shares' previous 1996/97 low of 210 yen marked on January 29, 1997.
Dealers said participants began to dump the bank's shares after learning that a yield difference between its bank debenture and that of Industrial Bank of Japan had widened to 2.6 percentage points.
One dealer said the sharp fall in the share dampened overall sentiment in the stock market in the morning.
Japanese government bond prices soared meanwhile on vague talk that NCB would hold an emergency news conference.
An NCB official denied the rumours but said the bank was preparing to issue a comment on its falling share price. He did not elaborate.
